activity.role: Daimyo and senior ruler of the Later Hōjō
activity.notes: Ujiyasu succeeded Hōjō Ujitsuna as third head of the Later Hōjō in 1541. He formally transferred the family headship to Ujimasa in 1559/1560, but contemporary and later accounts describe a continuing dual-rule arrangement in which Ujiyasu retained senior authority until his death in 1571. Following the project's Oda, Uesugi, Shimazu, Date, Mōri, Ōtomo and Imagawa conventions, the clan is represented as a territorial authority rather than as a sovereign 'Hōjō clan state'.

sources.title: 北条氏五代100年の歴史 — Odawara City
sources.citation_text: Odawara City's official chronology records Ujiyasu succeeding as third Hōjō head in 1541, transferring the headship to Ujimasa around 1560, and dying in 1571.

sources.title: Hojo Ujimasa — Japanese Wiki Corpus
sources.citation_text: This reference states that after the 1559 transfer of headship, a diarchy of Ujiyasu and Ujimasa continued until Ujiyasu's death.
